What

What Full-Excavation Stump Removal Involves

Stump removal by full excavation is different from stump grinding. Grinding takes the stump to 6–12 inches below grade and leaves the underground root system in place. Full excavation physically removes the entire stump and the major root ball, leaving a hole sized to the original root flare. It's the correct approach when new construction will sit over the stump location — footing, foundation, garage pad, in-ground pool shell, retaining wall, or hardscape patio — or when a land-use change requires the roots fully gone.

Most residential scenarios call for grinding instead — grinding is sufficient for grass, sod, pavers, small concrete pads, and most replant work, and it costs less. Aaron walks every job and confirms which method fits before you commit. When excavation is the right call, the crew handles the whole sequence: utility mark-out, extraction, backfill, and final grade.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Homeowners Choose Excavation

The scenarios where grinding won't do and the full root ball has to come out.

In-Ground Pool Shell

A pool shell or below-grade structure is going where the stump sits — the entire root ball has to be extracted first.

New Garage or Foundation

Foundation, footing, or garage-pad excavation over a former tree location. Grinding leaves roots that undermine the pour.

Hardscape Patio or Wall

Patio, retaining wall, or hardscape pad installation that requires full root-system removal for a stable base.

Land-Use Change

Rural re-grade or land-use change where the planned use specifically requires the stump and roots physically gone.

Common Stump Removal Questions

Stump Removal (Full Excavation) FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know before booking.

What's the difference between stump grinding and stump removal?
Grinding takes the stump to 6–12 inches below grade and leaves the underground root system in place. Removal by full excavation physically extracts the entire stump and the major root ball. Grinding is sufficient for grass, pavers, sod, and most replant scenarios; excavation is needed for new construction over the stump location.
How much does stump excavation cost?
Excavation pricing typically runs 2–4× grinding pricing for the same stump size, plus hauling and backfill. A stump that grinds for $250 might excavate for $700–$1,200 plus $200–$400 in backfill. Excavation is appropriate only when the planned land use specifically requires it.
Do I need a permit for stump excavation?
Possibly — depending on the village and the scope. Excavation that disturbs significant earth may trigger zoning review or building-department coordination. Roubic confirms the requirements during the free estimate.
Can grass grow over a ground stump?
Yes — grinding produces a chip-and-soil mix that supports grass seed within months, especially with optional topsoil backfill. The remaining underground root system decays over 5–10 years without affecting surface use.
Do you call for utility mark-out before excavating?
Always. Underground utility mark-out through the Ohio Utilities Protection Service (811) is mandatory for excavation, and Roubic schedules it at booking so the locate is complete before the excavator arrives.
